The release where the interface becomes our own, and robosystems.ai finishes becoming the platform's front door. Since v1.4.0 (September 19, 2026) the app has moved off the Flowbite component library onto UI primitives owned in `@robosystems/core`, gained a console drawer on every page and an Activity page for every graph, rebuilt its public pages around live product demos and an About page, and taken the MSA through an AWS Marketplace lane. The series went out as thirty-six patch releases; this file is the account of it as a whole.

## 🎨 The interface is ours

- **Every component the app renders now comes from `@robosystems/core/ui`,** the UI layer owned in the shared core package, in place of the Flowbite React library. Nothing you see changes: the cutover was gated on full-page screenshots of all forty-one routed pages in light and dark, on desktop and mobile, against the previous release, and every one rendered identically. Your dark-mode choice carries over untouched (#524)
- **The contact form's overlay is translucent again.** It had been solid since the Tailwind v4 upgrade (#524)

## 🗂️ Graphs, the console and activity

- **The console is a drawer at the bottom of every page,** and that drawer is the only way into it. Old `/console` links and bookmarks open it and land on Home (#448)
- **A graph has an Activity page:** every change made to it through the API, an MCP client or an AI operator, read from the mutation audit. Picking an AI operator's run shows what it was asked, what it answered or why it failed, how it ended, its credits and model calls, and the tools it called, above the changes it made (#448, #514)
- **The graph wizard holds Next while the selected tier is at capacity,** so the only way forward is Request access, instead of a Review step whose Create can only fail (#439)
- **The MCP page offers the RoboLedger connector address,** with the same sign-in recipes, when you own a graph that route serves; it stays off the SEC workspace, and the Claude directory listing for RoboSystems SEC is linked beside the ChatGPT plugin. The RoboLedger address is described as the custom connector it is (#452, #465, #493)
- **Usage shows only the limits the platform enforces,** and a repository subscription is described as it works (#505)

## 🔐 Sign-in, consent and billing

- **The consent screen reads the graph you can't reach.** When a connector pins a graph you don't subscribe to or can't read, the page says so and offers the way in, with Allow disabled; a default graph never overwrites a choice you made (#436, #512)
- **The cross-app sign-in bridge is bound to the browser that started it** (#518)
- **Billing says what happens to the unused period.** An immediate graph delete credits it, to the account balance on a card-billed plan or to the invoice on an invoiced plan; cancelling a member's repository seat cancels that seat, and each card says whose seat it is; the billing panels stay mounted while billing data reloads, so a tier change reports its outcome (#434, #502, #515, #516)

## 🌐 Public site, pricing and legal

- **Live demos on the homepage and the platform page.** The static previews are replaced by animated product demos: the hero shows a company's own numbers beside its peers and the public record, the platform page runs one continuous demo across graph management and the console, and the console is drawn as the bottom drawer it is. The demos run on the runtime shared with the product sites, so the three no longer drift (#441, #442, #443, #446, #466, #468, #469)
- **An About page** at robosystems.ai/about: why RoboSystems exists, what it makes, who builds it, and the companies behind it, with the founder profile the product sites link to (#424, #425, #447, #470)
- **Positioned as the platform, not a filing tool.** The homepage leads with your company, the companies around it and the public record in one knowledge graph; the SEC repository section sits below the applications it serves and deep-links its pricing; the console copy says it makes changes; the enterprise and pricing pages say what graph isolation is: a dedicated graph-database instance per graph (#426, #430, #444, #445, #454, #488, #501)
- **Dedicated Deployment can be bought as an AWS Marketplace private offer.** The MSA (v2.3) gains Schedule C for Marketplace purchases, defines what the Schedule B fees cover, and licenses customers to say they run on RoboSystems; the repository carries an Apache 2.0 `NOTICE` with the trademark attribution, and the Terms agree with it (#437, #438, #449, #450)
- **Pricing claims match the plans.** Starter no longer claims unlimited MCP access (#487)
- **Search engines and answer engines.** `/llms.txt` maps the site for language models, the Organization and founder carry stable `@id`s the product sites reference, and the Research and RoboLedger content it once hosted lives on its sibling sites (#432, #433)
- **The API reference renders what the spec says:** tagged-union request bodies get a field table per arm, every example becomes a numbered sample, and field limits show (#440)

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- **Deployed builds get the production content-security policy.** The list was chosen by request hostname, which a deployed server does not report; it is chosen by environment now. This also completes the Data Lake browser-upload fix (#431)
- **Refusals show as refusals.** The SDK resolves HTTP errors instead of throwing, so pages reported a refused create, checkout or backup as success or empty data; they now surface the refusal, through the shared error helpers (#428)
- **Activity's next page lands on the graph it was fetched for,** not the one you switched to while it loaded (#508)
- Email verification redirects, the OAuth consent default never wins over a click, and the GraphQL docs page's curl sample escapes its body with `JSON.stringify` (#422, #436)

## 🔒 Hardening

- Client IP attribution for the contact and support forms is hardened behind the CDN, and the blog's social cards are cached at the edge (#427)
- The cross-app sign-in bridge is bound to the product app's browser (#518)

## 🔧 Infrastructure

- **`@robosystems/client` 1.17.2 → 2.35.0,** crossing the client's 2.0 line. **`@robosystems/core` 0.9.5 → 0.19.0,** carrying the console drawer, the Activity page's audit reads, the demo runtime, the error helpers and, in 0.18, the owned UI layer (#423, #428, #435, #455, #467, #478, #491, #492, #494, #496, #498, #499, #500, #507, #509, #514, #518, #524, #525)
- **Flowbite, flowbite-react and the `deepmerge-ts` override they forced are gone** from the dependency tree, and the image no longer copies the generated class list. `npm audit`'s remaining findings are one `minimatch` advisory reached only through the eslint toolchain, dev-only (#524)
- **The app runs on Node 26,** the active LTS since October 28: the image base, the workflows, `engines` and the type definitions move together, and the vitest workers turn off Node's own Web Storage so the browser-style storage the tests use stays jsdom's (#525)
- **Next 16.4.** vitest 4.1 and Vite 8.3; vitest 5 is held until its 5.1 line (#504, #510, #522)
- **A second compute route.** App Runner is closed to new AWS customers, so the deploy workflow offers ECS Express Mode beside it for a fork deploying into a fresh account; App Runner stays the default (#451)
- **Permissions boundaries** on every IAM role the app's stacks create (#479)
- **CI and images:** Docker Hub publishes over OIDC instead of a stored token, base images pull authenticated from ECR Public, the hosted runner image is pinned, and the build's credential scope is narrowed (#453, #456, #461, #462, #463, #464, #477)
- **For forks and self-hosters:** the app requires Node 26 and `@robosystems/core` 0.19.0 or later, and a per-call Flowbite `theme` object has no equivalent; the Modal, Card and Alert primitives accept a partial `theme` merged over the defaults (#524)

## 📦 Deploy notes

- **No API upgrade is required.** Everything this release reads is served by the API already in production, including the operator run record, the consent screen's graph-access read and the billing credits.
- **The production image moves to Node 26.** Nothing in the stack changes with it; watch the first run's logs as with any runtime change.
- **No pending CloudFormation changes.** The series added the ECS Express template and the permissions-boundary parameter, and both reached production with the v1.4.x patches.
- **One secret added during the series,** already set here: the `ORIGIN_VERIFY_SECRET` repository secret (#427). A fork needs it.
